one_liner: Qt plus FFmpeg playback library with hardware decoding and GPU YUV rendering; one author anecdote claims 10% less CPU than VLC.
what_it_does: QtAV is a media playback framework for Qt applications: an AVPlayer object demuxes and decodes through FFmpeg (or Libav) and hands frames to pluggable renderers (OpenGL/ES2 widgets, QPainter, QML Video item, and since August 2025 a contributed Vulkan renderer) and audio outputs (OpenAL and others). It adds hardware decoders (DXVA2, D3D11, VA-API, VDA/VideoToolbox, CUDA, CedarX), libavfilter and custom filters, subtitles via FFmpeg or libass, frame capture, and a QtMultimedia-like QML API. It is a library for writing a player, not a drop-in replacement for the VLC application or libVLC's API.
how_it_is_fast: The claimed savings come from keeping decoded frames on the GPU: zero-copy interop renders hardware-decoded surfaces directly (VDA via IOSurface with NV12 into GL_TEXTURE_RECTANGLE, VA-API via EGL dma-buf or GLX, DXVA and CUDA interop), and YUV-to-RGB conversion runs in OpenGL/ES2 shaders, including 16-bit textures for 10-bit (Hi10P) video. When frames must come back to system memory, an 'OptimizedCopy' path copies from write-combined GPU memory with SSE4.1 streaming loads (_mm_stream_load_si128 through a 4 KB cache block, CopyFrame_SSE4.cpp), with an SSE2 fallback. The 10-bit VLC anecdote most likely reflects shader-based 10-bit rendering versus a CPU conversion in VLC at the time, but the source does not say (inference).
when_to_use: Maintaining an existing Qt 5 application that already embeds QtAV and runs against FFmpeg 4.x or older
Qt 5 desktop or embedded players that need hardware decode with zero-copy OpenGL rendering on VA-API, VideoToolbox, DXVA or CUDA
Rendering 10-bit (Hi10P) video through OpenGL ES2 shaders on Qt 5 targets
Studying a compact, LGPL reference for GPU interop and SSE4.1 USWC frame readback inside a Qt pipeline
when_not_to_use: New projects: the author states he no longer develops QtAV; the last release is 1.13.0 (2019-07-11) and 2025 commits are a contributor's Vulkan renderer only
FFmpeg 5 or newer: issue #1377 (open) reports removed APIs (av_bitstream_filter_*, const AVCodec*) break the build, and a community patch built but crashed after a few frames
Qt 6: issue #1406 (open, no maintainer reply) reports QtAV does not build with Qt 6.2; the CMake build looks for Qt5 only
When you need measured performance guarantees: the only number is a 2014 single-phone forum anecdote, and a user report says VLC plays full-HD more smoothly
Closed-source static linking without LGPL compliance work: the library is LGPL-2.1, the player example GPL-3.0, and FFmpeg's licence applies on top

integration.form: shared lib (QtAV, QtAVWidgets) plus QML plugin
integration.dependencies: Qt 4.8 or Qt 5 (CMake build: Qt 5 only), FFmpeg 1.0 to 4.x or Libav 9+ (libavcodec, libavformat, libavutil, libswscale, libswresample or libavresample), optional OpenAL, libass, VA-API, CUDA, Vulkan
integration.min_toolchain: Not stated; CMake 2.8.11+ or qmake, compiler that builds Qt 5; no C++ standard is pinned in CMakeLists.txt
integration.platforms: Windows (DXVA2, D3D11, CUDA), Linux (VA-API, CUDA), macOS and iOS (VDA, VideoToolbox), Android, Raspberry Pi and Allwinner CedarX; OptimizedCopy needs SSE4.1 on x86 or NEON for CedarV
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; AVPlayer is a QObject driven by Qt's event loop that runs its own demux, decode and output threads

gotchas: Zero-copy is backend- and GPU-specific: the wiki says NVIDIA GPUs do not support EGL with VA-API, AMD is untested, DXVA 0-copy in desktop OpenGL works only on some newer Intel GPUs and is 'not stable', and VA-API zero-copy may not work on the vdpau backend.
OptimizedCopy's SSE4.1 path is documented as not working on some GPUs (e.g. NVIDIA GS8400) and as crashing with VDA.
Several advertised backends (VDPAU, some D3D11 and CUDA paths, RPI and Cedarv EGL) exist only in the author's successor mdk-sdk, which is binary-only and key-licensed, not in QtAV.

The performance claim cannot be checked: forum.qt.io/post/21312 does not resolve here (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so the 10% figure is from search snippets of a 2014 author post with no VLC version, decoder path, file or method.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the video-audio siblings is a player framework: dav1d, edge264, rivet-h26x and vvdec are decoders and GStreamer is a general pipeline framework; pick QtAV only when you need a ready Qt/QML playback widget and can stay on Qt 5 with FFmpeg 4.x, otherwise use GStreamer or an FFmpeg-based decoder directly.
verified_claims_summary: The only number is the author's own 2014 Qt-forum report that QtAV used about 10% less CPU than VLC playing a 10-bit H.264 file on an HTC Butterfly S phone, with no VLC version, decoder path, video, build or methodology, read from search snippets because the forum is unreachable. The wiki's claims ('better than any other players' for VDA, CUDA DirectCopy 'faster than potplayer, lavfilters+mpc') carry no numbers.
status_note: Stale: the author stopped development (README points to his key-licensed mdk-sdk), last release 1.13.0 in 2019, last commit 2025-08-15 (contributor Vulkan renderer), and it does not build with FFmpeg 5+ or Qt 6 without third-party patches; LGPL-2.1 source remains copyable.
